solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secure key left in church

blocks.note: C is a musical key
L is the usual abbreviation for left
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone locks up the church, keeping its key safe and leaving it inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is simply the letters IN, read in order between the abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to secure or settle it conclusively, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Battle putting outer garment round bishop after Mass

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the garment's letters enclose the others
after says the bishop's letter follows the Mass letter in the order read

blocks.note: a coat is worn over other clothes
M is the physics symbol for mass
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric dresses for a fight by wrapping a coat round himself after attending Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: M then B sit together inside CO-AT. 'Mass' looks religious beside 'bishop' but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is armed fighting between forces, a direct synonym for battle.

clue.text: Reprice a label confusingly priceless?

indicators.note: something done confusingly is jumbled, so the letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, all thirteen

explanation.surface: A shop assistant muddles the job of putting a new price label on something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that priceless is defined loosely: something that cannot be replaced has no price.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priceless is beyond value and so cannot be substituted, which is what irreplaceable means.

clue.text: Admit using back of shelf in cooking scones

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the last one is kept
cooking food transforms it, so the letters are mixed into a new order
in places the selected letter inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
the final letter of shelf

explanation.surface: A baker owns up to taking something off the back of the shelf while making scones.
explanation.walkthrough: SCONES is rearranged to CON-ESS and F is slipped into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to admit a fault or wrongdoing, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Shopkeeper increasingly offensive in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

blocks.note: grosser means more vulgar or offensive

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's language keeps getting ruder.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a person who keeps a shop selling food and household goods.

clue.text: Fashions run a very long time

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
ages is an informal phrase for a very long time

explanation.surface: Fashion trends stay popular for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rages are crazes or passing fashions, as in 'all the rage', a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Complete attention unsettled innocent actor

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen fodder letters

explanation.surface: A nervous, naive actor loses focus on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentration is the act of giving one's full mental focus to something, an exact phrase synonym.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved at gift being unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the opening letter of the word is taken away

blocks.note: a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that a present has been left unwrapped and ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'at': you resent something, just as you feel aggrieved at it.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitterness or indignation about it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: River in US Atlantic state right for sailor

indicators.note: in places the river's letter inside the name of the state

blocks.note: Maine is a US state on the Atlantic coast
R is the abbreviation for river
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A river in Maine is just right for a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside MA-INE, then a second R is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who navigates or works on a ship.

clue.text: Squabbles about eats in disorderly behaviour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: rows are noisy quarrels
dines means eats a meal

explanation.surface: Arguments over meals lead to unruly conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like the container signal but is only the link to the definition; 'about' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiness is noisy, rough and disorderly conduct, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Closely related group of antelopes around centre of Senegal

indicators.note: around means the animals' name surrounds the selected letter
the centre of a word is its middle letter only

blocks.note: gnus are African antelopes, also called wildebeest
the fourth of seven letters sits in the middle

explanation.surface: A herd of related antelopes gathers around the middle of Senegal.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside G-NUS. 'Closely related group of antelopes' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops before 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification rank of closely related species, so a closely related group.

clue.text: Plentiful specimens uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so first and last letters are lost

blocks.note: samples are specimens taken for testing

explanation.surface: Plenty of specimens have been exposed for examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, an adjective synonym for plentiful.

clue.text: People in general forbidding cowboy film

blocks.note: we can stand for people generally, as in 'we all need sleep'
stern means severe or forbidding in manner

explanation.surface: Audiences find a grim cowboy film hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forbidding' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning grim.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a genre of film set in the American Old West, typically featuring cowboys.

clue.text: Having given up drink, missing carrying can

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: absent means missing or not present
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A former drinker is no longer seen holding a can.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from something, especially alcohol, so has given up drink.

clue.text: Couple chasing me round for hug

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
chasing means following behind, so the pair word comes after

blocks.note: taken as written
a brace is a pair, especially of game birds

explanation.surface: A pair chase after me, wanting a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: ME becomes EM, followed by BRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, holding someone closely in one's arms, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Consequence of cups having heat, not cold

indicators.note: not means take away, and cold is the letter used on taps

blocks.note: taken as written
having heat means being hot
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Hot rather than cold cups have some consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: CUPS plus HOT, then the C for cold is removed from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final result or outcome of something, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Selective eater's struggle eating what could be boiled or poached

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one word encloses another

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

blocks.clueFragment: what could be boiled or poached
blocks.note: eggs are cooked by boiling or poaching

explanation.surface: A fussy eater struggles to eat a boiled or poached egg.
explanation.walkthrough: EGG sits inside V-IE. The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie, informal for vegetarian, chooses not to eat meat, making them a selective eater.

clue.text: Pair escape from passage opening

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
to elude is to escape from

explanation.surface: Two people escape from an opening in a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage opening' sounds like a doorway, but means an introductory piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an introductory musical movement, so a passage that opens a larger work.

clue.text: Total put into circulation

blocks.note: first meaning: complete or absolute
second meaning: to pass counterfeit money or forged documents

explanation.surface: An accountant puts a total sum into circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter is an adjective meaning absolute, and also a legal verb for passing off forged currency.

clue.text: British youth with English knife

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a lad is a youth or boy
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A young British man is carrying an English knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is the cutting part of a knife, and by extension a knife or sword itself.

clue.text: I bath when changing clothes

indicators.note: changing means altering the form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes a bath while getting changed out of their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing clothes' reads as one phrase, but 'changing' is the signal and 'clothes' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a distinctive garment, such as a nun's or a riding habit, so clothes.

clue.text: Arrangement of letters in text resetting G in caps

indicators.note: resetting means setting again in another way, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A typesetter resets a G in capitals in a passage of text.
explanation.walkthrough: The typesetting surface makes 'in' look like a container signal, but it is just two letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacing is the distribution of gaps between characters and words in printed text.

clue.text: Those ones accepting our heartless abstract reasoning

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one word holds another
without its heart a word loses its middle, keeping just the outside letters

blocks.note: they means those people
the outside letters of the three-letter word

explanation.surface: Cold-hearted people accept our abstract arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' sounds like a judgement on the people, but it strips the middle letter from 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a system of ideas explaining something, reasoning in the abstract rather than practice.

clue.text: Spiritual gathering in main new Anglican organisation

blocks.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A spiritual meeting is held in a major new Anglican body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun meaning the sea, as in 'Spanish Main'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which people try to contact spirits of the dead.
